extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural staff, grant applicants, awardee institutions, and other stakeholders in NIH grants administration
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Office of Policy for Extramural Research Administration (OPERA) responsibilities, divisions, and functions relating to grants management policy, compliance, intellectual property, OMB clearances, and closeout activities across NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: stewardship of NIH extramural funds
rubrics_metrics.description: OPERA provides leadership and oversight in grants management policy and compliance, intellectual property, and OMB clearances to the extramural research community and NIH extramural staff to promote effective stewardship of NIH extramural funds in support of health research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames OPERA's overarching goal and priority: policies and actions should promote effective stewardship of public funds supporting health research.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH extramural policies and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop, maintain, and interpret NIH policies and procedures for administering extramural grants and cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes creating policy language, issuing guidance, and standardizing administrative practices across NIH institutes and centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Grants Policy Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The authoritative policy document governing administration of NIH grants and cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPERA is responsible for aspects of the Grants Policy Statement; this serves as a formal standard for grant administration requirements and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH grant and training application forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Management and oversight of application forms used for NIH grant and training submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that application forms meet policy requirements and reflect current programmatic and compliance needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Property / Bayh-Dole implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Development, implementation, and monitoring of extramural intellectual property policies including invention reporting under the Bayh-Dole Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers institutional obligations for invention reporting, IP policy alignment across NIH, and oversight to ensure Bayh-Dole compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB clearances under the Paperwork Reduction Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Management of Office of Management and Budget (OMB) clearance requirements for NIH public information collection activities under the Paperwork Reduction Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures NIH collections of information from the public comply with PRA requirements (e.g., obtain necessary OMB approvals) and coordinates clearance activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants compliance and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance external compliance with policy and legislative mandates and enhance compliance oversight by recipient institutions to ensure efficient and effective management of extramural resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes evaluating recipient institutions' compliance systems, responding to compliance issues, and implementing oversight activities to protect public funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial conflict of interest oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and compliance responsibilities related to financial conflicts of interest for NIH grants and extramural research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involves setting and interpreting standards to identify, manage, and report conflicts of interest to maintain research integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH implementation of federal-wide initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing and aligning NIH policy and practice with federal-wide initiatives that affect extramural research administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination and adoption of cross-government initiatives that impact grants policy, compliance, reporting, or administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Clearance Branch (OMB clearance control point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Serves as NIH control point for OMB clearance functions concerning public information collection activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts as the central reviewer and coordinator for PRA/OMB clearance submissions and communications for NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Transactions policy coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: OPERA is the central point of contact for Other Transactions and coordinates and manages Other Transactions policies and activities across NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines policy and processes for non-traditional agreements (Other Transactions) and supports NIH components in their use and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Grants Policy (DGP) role
rubrics_metrics.description: Develops, executes, and interprets NIH policies for administering financial assistance (grants and cooperative agreements) and provides policy guidance for NIH extramural staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides leadership and support to address emerging issues and standardize grants administration practices within NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Grant Systems Integration responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Performs analysis and develops business processes and functionality for implementing and automating grants policy business process requirements; serves as central coordination for closeout activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on translating policy into system requirements and workflows, and coordinating technical implementation to support policy compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems Policy Branch (SPB) liaison function
rubrics_metrics.description: Serves as the liaison between OPERA and system owners at NIH and across the Federal government to implement policies and compliance initiatives in NIH electronic systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures system-level changes reflect policy directives and support compliance and data collection requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout Center function
rubrics_metrics.description: Central coordination and receipt location for closeout reports; provides closeout services for grants and cooperative agreements for the Office of the Director and 24 NIH institutes and centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes closeout submission processes and acts as the central point for processing closeout documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Financial Report Reconciliation and Financial Closeout Support Center (FFRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversees the review, acceptance, and ultimate approval of Federal Financial Reports (FFRs) submitted to NIH by grant recipients and supports financial closeout activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides reconciliation and approval workflows for FFRs, addressing financial reporting accuracy and facilitating final closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Grants Compliance and Oversight (DGCO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focal point to advance external compliance with policy and legislative mandates, enhance compliance oversight by recipient institutions, and evaluate efficient and effective management of extramural resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also develops, implements, and monitors extramural IP policies and invention reporting under Bayh-Dole; leads enforcement and oversight activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access Support Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Responds to questions from the public and recipients about the NIH Public Access policy and helps NIH recipients bring their scientific papers into compliance with the policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides assistance and guidance to ensure publications resulting from NIH support meet public access requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Compliance of Foreign Interference, Research Misconduct, Harassment and Intellectual Property (FIRMH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advises NIH leadership on the direction and management of extramural research compliance activities that cut across NIH’s mission, covering grant policy issues related to foreign government interference, research misconduct and harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinates policy and response strategies for complex cross-cutting compliance risks including foreign interference and misconduct.
